content.text:
Done. Tests green (`BUILD SUCCESS`, 2/2).

I agree with the finding and applied it. `Soundex` is a pure, domain-agnostic standard string algorithm — a sibling of `Luhn` and `Hashes`, both of which the codebase keeps in `function/common` (and `Luhn` too has only owner-domain consumers), so "single consumer is in owner" was the wrong reason for its placement.

Changes:
- Moved `Soundex` to `org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.common`.
- Made it `public` (like `Luhn`/`Hashes`) and dropped the "kept out of the function classes / one public method" javadoc note, which only applies to the owner-package helpers neighboring function classes — matching how `Luhn`/`Hashes` omit it. Reworded the class javadoc to the `common` style (leads with what it computes and why, plus the "pinned so both arms agree" note).
- Added `import ...common.Soundex` in `IdentityKey` (right next to its existing `Hashes` import) and in `AssignOwnerPossibleDuplicate`; the `{@link Soundex}` references now resolve through those imports.

No logic or acceptance behaviour changed — the algorithm is byte-for-byte identical, just relocated.
